title: transfer-custody answers 201 with no anchor when the lifecycle anchor call is refused: seven anchor-less 201s on kintsugi
description:
**BLUF:** `POST /api/documents/{id}/transfer-custody` answers 201 with `anchorId` null when the anchoring call it makes after writing the custody event is refused, so a caller cannot tell a transfer that was anchored from one that was not without a second call. On kintsugi on 2026-10-26, seven accepted transfers for one document were each followed, 8 to 37 ms later, by a `POST /api/anchors` answered 400; the document has 0 anchor rows and none of its 7 custody events records an anchor. Raised from the KS-1402 read-back (comment 06ba4a1f); KS-1402 stays open and is not changed by this ticket.

## What the code does at develop `249be7c8cd14`

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts` lines 1458 to 1472: `emitLifecycleAnchor` throws on a non-ok anchoring answer, its catch logs "Lifecycle anchor emission failed" and returns `{ anchorId: null, txHash: null, status: 'pending' }` (the comment at line 1466 says the caller falls back to `/api/anchors`).
* The same file, lines 2506 to 2525: the transfer-custody handler awaits that call and then answers 201 with `transfer.anchorId` and `transfer.anchor.status` taken from it, whatever it returned.

## What was measured on kintsugi (read-only, 2026-10-29, comment 06ba4a1f)

* 7 `custody_events` rows for one document, all with an empty anchor transaction; 7 audit rows `POST .../transfer-custody` answered 201; 7 `anchors.create` requests answered 400, the only such 400s in the trail; the anchor table holds 0 rows for the document (control: another document holds 1).
* Build: develop `1ae6f17d19a8`.

## Not measured, not decided

* The reason the anchor calls were refused (the Invalid DID text is the likely cause, but originate's log for 26 Oct is not on the box).
* Whether a refused anchor should make the route answer a non-2xx, or whether 201 with a `pending` anchor is the intended contract: nothing read rules on it.

## Related

KS-1402 (the measurement), KS-1811 (the same seven events seen as self-transfers), KS-1175 and KS-1813 (the did:jwk schema and pattern), KS-1384 (anchor rows per document).

## Searched

Searched `transfer-custody`, `custody event`, `anchorless`, `anchor-less`, `users/lookup`, `Lifecycle anchor emission failed`, `Invalid DID`, `did:jwk`, `no ref in payload`, `anchors fallback` and `transfer-custody+anchor+201` over title, description and comments (archived included; positive control `msgpackr` hits KS-1379, a random token 0): 0 open tickets that cover this; KS-1811 covers the repeat custody event only, KS-1402 carries the measurement.
